correctness.rationale: Let p(z)=sum_{k=0}^d a_k z^k. Its squared modulus on each radius r is a trigonometric polynomial with modes [-d,d]; a 2d-point regular ring DFT recovers every mode |k|<d and aliases only the conjugate top pair into 2r^d Re(a_d conj(a_0)e^{idφ}). Two rings give independent real linear equations in the same complex v=a_d conj(a_0) iff sin(d(φ2−φ1))≠0. With that condition all full-circle intensities on both radii are determined. If p,q have same two full-circle intensities, the rational R=p/q satisfies R(z)overline{R(r_j²/conj?)}=1 in the standard rational-reflection identity; eliminating j yields invariance of R#(w) under dilation r2²/r1²≠1, forcing rational R constant, then unit modulus. Zeros are handled as rational identities; p=0 gives q=0 since 2d>d sample zeros. When radii coincide, p=z−t and q=(t/r)z−r with t≠r have same full-circle modulus, not global phase. When angular sine vanishes, p=1+i exp(−idφ1)z^d and q=1−i exp(−idφ1)z^d have identical samples, not phase equivalents. These prove sharp iff for every d≥1, including vanishing coefficients. Source checker.py finite degrees 1–12 supports, does not replace analytic proof.
